When I return to the living room, neither Tohsaka nor Illya is there.

“…Did they both go back to their rooms?”

“…They must’ve gone to their rooms.”

pages.en:
That makes sense.

They are busy trying to reproduce this “Jeweled Sword.”

My part comes only after they finish the replica they are fashioning after the original.

Until then, my duty is to draw as much magecraft experience as I can from Archer's left arm.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Oh, yeah.
They’re busy trying to reproduce the gem sword.
I can only help after they make a replica similar to the original.
My job for now is to draw out as much of Archer’s experience as I can.

おそらくは半々で投影は成る。
アーチャーの真似事をして、本物の真似事をさらに作り上げるワケだ。

pages.en:
“I am the bone of my sword—”

…A singular incantation belonging to someone else—to Archer—surged backward into me with the pain.

If I sink into myself through that strangely easy refrain, my chances of succeeding at Projection rise dramatically.

I can probably manage it one time in two.

I imitate Archer in order to fashion yet another imitation of the genuine article.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I am the bone of my sword, huh?”
…Archer’s original spell, which flowed into me along with the pain.
If I use this strangely familiar incantation to look within myself, my rate of success greatly increases.
Projection now succeeds half the time.
I’m copying Archer to make a copy of something.

それを“一つの幻想”に仕上げたいというのなら、この腕の力を借りる他はない。

pages.en:
“—But anything I make that way is still a fake.”

…Projection is replication, yet what it creates is identical to the original.

What Shirou Emiya creates is no more than an inferior delusion.

If I mean to perfect it into a single fantasy, I have no choice but to borrow the power of this arm.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
But I can only create a fake.”
…Projection is reproducing something identical to the original.
Emiya Shirou can only create an inferior imagination.
The only way to create a phantasm is with the arm’s help.

“—Gh.”

Self-destruction.

It is not a matter of the arm poisoning me once I use it.

Using it throws the switch on a bomb.

Use it, and the end will come without fail.

!”
Suicide.
It’s not that poison will come into me once I use it.
A bomb will be switched on once I use it.
A sure end will come once I use it.

pages.en:
The image of a gun's hammer.

There is a pistol inside my brain.

The muzzle points outward, away from my brain, but the trigger remains enclosed within it.

This pistol must be the image behind the “time bomb” Kotomine described.
pages.mirrorMoon:
An image of a firing hammer.
There’s a gun in my brain.
The muzzle is pointed outward, but the trigger is still there.
This image must be the time bomb Kotomine spoke of.

“…Then if I could take the gun out of my head, using the arm wouldn't throw the switch.”

No. The switch itself—the thing that would otherwise be thrown—would be outside me.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“But if I can take the gun out of my head, the switch won’t go off even if I use it.”
No, the switch itself will be outside my body.

I turn on the television.

I need to know what has become of last night's incident, so I watch the news through the heaviness in my body.

I have to know what happened yesterday, so I watch the news.

Finding the right channel is easy.

pages.en:
—A mass disappearance of unknown cause.

—Residents remain unaccounted for in forty separate buildings.

—Not one neighboring resident who escaped harm noticed that the people next door had vanished.

—Nearly sixty people, none of whom are ever likely to return.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The unexplained disappearances.
There are over forty houses with missing residents.
None of the survivors noticed their neighbors’ disappearance.
And almost sixty people will never return.

Even then, could you forgive?

The thing that did it.

Yourself, for looking away.

Could you truly forgive either one?

Will you still be able to forgive it when the time comes?
Will you be able to forgive the thing that’s causing it?
Will you be able to forgive yourself for overlooking it?

The television goes dark.

The newscast that had been spelling out the toll with perfect clarity—

“Don't be an idiot.

“You and I aren't decent enough to start regretting things after they've already happened.”

—is cut off without mercy by Tohsaka, who appeared without my noticing.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The TV switches off.
The news that has been informing me of the incident is…
“Don’t be stupid.
We’re not decent enough people to mourn over what’s already done.”
…Mercilessly cut off by Tohsaka.

“…Hmph. I only wanted a fresh start myself. You're incidental, Shirou. Incidental.”

When someone goes to the trouble of showing concern this clumsily, the only thing to do is accept it gratefully.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Heh. I just wanted to get myself together. You just happened to be here, okay?”
If this is how she wants to show her concern for me, I’ll just have to accept it.

Time passes.

Tohsaka and I sit facing each other, drinking tea in silence and doing nothing at all.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Time passes.
We just drink the tea silently.

I don’t feel nervous for some reason.
I rather feel relaxed.
…This is purely speculation, but…
Could Tohsaka be one of those girls that soothes the atmosphere?

“Oh, I was thinking to myself. We’ve never sat around doing nothing like this, right?
Whenever we’re together, we talk about the Holy Grail War. So I thought we had a pretty savage relationship.”

“O-Of course it has! That's how we met! What do you expect us to discuss under the circumstances—the next exam or our favorite restaurants?”

“What? No, I think we're fine as we are. A relationship where neither of us can let down our guard feels right for us.”

And yet our ability to relax together like this is so oddly out of balance that I cannot help finding it funny.

“I-I can’t help it. That’s how it all started! Or what? Do you want me to talk about what might come up on the finals or what stores I like to go to?”
“Huh? I guess it’s fine as is. I think this dangerous relationship is suited for us.”
But we were so relaxed that it felt weird and funny.

“Well, you're right. That is how it began.

Seen that way, becoming a Master has given me one more thing to be grateful for.

Now I can stand and fight beside the girl I used to admire only from afar.

I can fight alongside the girl I’ve admired.

“Y-You knew me?”

When I stare and ask why, Tohsaka gives another rather embarrassed nod.

“Y-You knew me?”
Tohsaka nods with embarrassment.

“Th-That's impossible…! Did we talk sometime during our first year? I don't remember!”

“N-No, nothing like that.

“When I say I knew you, I mean it was entirely one-sided.

“You see, Shirou Emiya has become something of a trauma for me.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“N-No way…! Did we talk when we were in the first year!?”
“N-No.
I knew about you, but you didn’t know about me.
You’re one of my traumas.”

pages.ja:
「ト、トラウマってなんでさ！？」
なんかイヤだぞ、それ。
自分の知らないところで人の心に傷をつけていた、なんて事は、まあ、生きている以上は仕方ないとしてもだ。
その相手が三倍返し四倍返し上等な遠坂だっていうのは精神衛生上よろしくない！

pages.en:
“A trauma!? How!?”

I don't like the sound of that.

People inevitably hurt one another without ever realizing it. That is part of being alive.

But knowing the victim is Tohsaka—a firm believer in threefold or fourfold retaliation—is very bad for my peace of mind!
pages.mirrorMoon:
“W-Why!?”
I don’t like that.
I know it can’t be helped to hurt someone when you don’t know about it.
But it’s not good for my mental health to know that I’ve hurt Tohsaka, who likes to strike back three or four times as hard!

「なんでって、そんなのわたしが言いたいぐらいよ。
……いいわ。いい機会だから直接グチってあげる。
今から四年前の、ちょうど今ごろの話よ。貴方、どうしてだか知らないけど学校に残って、日が落ちるまでずっと走り高跳びやってた事があるでしょ」

pages.en:
“How? I would like to know that myself.

“…Fine. This is a good opportunity, so I'll complain to you directly.

“It happened four years ago, at about this time of year. For some reason, you stayed at school and practiced the high jump until sunset. You remember that, don't you?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I’m the one who wants to ask that.
…Fine, this is a good opportunity, so let me grumble a bit.
It happened around this time four years ago. I don’t know why, but you were there after school, doing running high jumps until the sun set, right?”

The unexpected question leaves me staring blankly.

Not because of what she asked.

What shocks me is that Sakura once described precisely the same thing.

Huh?”
I’m taken aback by the unexpected question.
It’s not the question itself.
What surprised me is that Sakura was talking about the exact same thing.

pages.en:
“J-Just so you know, I happened to be there by chance. I only went to your school on student-council business. We weren't merely in different classes—we attended different schools.”

“Right. I heard you went to the same school as Issei.”

“I-It was just a coincidence, okay? I went to your school because of a matter related to the Student Council. I was in a different school, let alone class.”
“Yeah. I heard that you went to the same school as Issei.”

pages.ja: 「そ、あいつとはその頃からの腐れ縁。前はわたしが副会長で、あいつが会長だったの。四年間も顔あわせて言い合ってたら、どっちも気に食わない天敵同士だって理解できたけど」

pages.en: “Yes. Our rotten connection goes back that far. I was vice president and he was president. Four years of arguing whenever we saw each other taught both of us that we're natural enemies who simply can't stand one another.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Yeah, we’ve known each other since then. I was the vice-president and he was the president. After four years spent fighting, we found out that we can’t get along.”

“…I see. I never realized the feud went back that far.”

That explains it.

I always thought there was something abnormal about Issei's attitude toward Tohsaka.

Hmm. It feels as though one mystery has thawed—or perhaps frozen even more solidly. Something like that.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…I see. So it was a long relationship.”
I finally understand now.
I knew Issei’s attitude towards Tohsaka was not normal.
Well, the mystery is unraveled… actually, it seems even more tangled now.

」

I have objections to her method of identification, but I keep them to myself.

I want to say something about what she thought about me, but I stay quiet.

わたしは、あの馬鹿みたいにずっと走ってた誰かを、羨ましいと思ってたんだって」

pages.en:
“…And at that moment, I was shocked. Three years had passed, yet I recognized at a glance a complete stranger whose name I'd never known, who attended another school, and whom I'd dismissed as an utter fool.

“Only then, three years later, did I realize that he had left a wound in me.

“I had envied that nameless boy who kept running like an idiot.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…And I was shocked at that time. There was this stranger who went to a different school that I’d considered stupid all this time, but I remembered him even after three years.
And I finally realized that you’ve been giving me damage all this time.
I found out I was jealous of this guy that kept on running like an idiot.”

pages.jaRuby: 「そうね。わたしは羨ましかったんじゃなくて、負けたって思った。……そいつが少しでも跳べるんだって希望を持って走っていたんなら良かった。そんなコトなら素通りして、さっさと家に帰ってた」

pages.jaRuby:

“…But he knew it was impossible.

“He knew nothing he did would make it possible, and still he kept trying. …As though even if it were futile, he believed the attempt itself meant something.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…But even he knew it was impossible.
He knew nothing would change that, but he kept trying. It’s as if he believed the effort was what mattered.”

そのあたり冷めてるっていうか、ひどい人間なのよ、わたし。綺礼は非道ではなく機械的だって言ってたけど」

“…Honestly, I could never devote myself to something so pointless.

“I've always been that way. It's in my nature to weigh whether something can succeed and withdraw cleanly if I decide it's beyond me. I don't attempt what I cannot do, and I don't feel inadequate or disappointed about it.

“I'm cold that way. A rather terrible person. Kirei said I wasn't heartless so much as mechanical.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…To be honest, I can’t do such a thing.
I’ve always been like that. I determine whether or not something is possible. If I know it’s impossible for me, I quickly give up. I don’t try what I can’t do, and I never regret it or think I’m powerless because of it.
I’m cold like that. I’m a terrible person. Kirei called it machine-like instead of cruel.”

pages.jaRuby:

Despite what she says, Tohsaka is not disparaging herself.

She takes pride in being that person and has confidence in it.

She’s proud of how she is.

pages.ja: 「けど、時々思うことだってある。事の成否なんて考えず、ただ物事に打ち込める事が出来たら、それはどんなに純粋な事なんだろうって」
pages.jaRuby: 「けど、時々思うことだってある。事の成否なんて考えず、ただ物事に打ち込める事が出来たら、それはどんなに純粋な事なんだろうって」

pages.mirrorMoon: “But I do sometimes think how pure it’d be to just keep trying without a thought for whether it’s possible.”

pages.en:
“…Well, I was still young enough to be troubled by questions like that. Imagine suddenly seeing someone who was your complete opposite. Of course it would come as a shock.

pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Well, as a child, it’s shocking to see someone that’s completely the opposite of you, right?
That’s why it was traumatic. That guy who foolishly kept running was…”

夢見るような顔で、そんなコトを呟いた。
